text:
Tugtainer

 

Tugtainer is a self-hosted application that automates Docker container updates. It is distributed as-is and is not intended for production use. Important data needs regular backups.

Automatic updates are disabled by default.

 Upgrading to 2.x

 [!WARNING] 
 - Self-update from 1.x to 2.x is not supported, and the database stays compatible. Recreate the app container from ghcr.io/quenary/tugtainer:2 and keep the /tugtainer volume.
 - The 2.x agent API is not compatible with 1.x. Recreate every remote agent from ghcr.io/quenary/tugtainer-agent:2 in the same change.
 - 2.x images are published for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only. linux/arm/v7 is no longer published.

 Main features

- Web UI with authentication
- Multiple hosts
- Docker Swarm (manager detection, service checks, rolling updates, logs)
- Socket proxy
- Crontab scheduling
- Notifications
- Per-container check-only or auto-update
- Manual and scheduled check and update
- Healthcheck monitoring with restarts and notifications
- Manual and scheduled image pruning
- Linked containers (Compose and custom labels)
- Private registries
- Basic container control (start, stop, and the rest)
- Container inspect and logs

 Deploy

 Quick start

The app starts from docker-compose.app.yml or from:

 

On the first start the container logs a one-time setup code ( docker logs tugtainer ). The password is set with that code within 5 minutes. An expired code requires a restart. See Auth.

The app cannot update an agent or a socket-proxy: those containers carry the Docker API connection. A Compose project that mixes them with containers set to auto-update fails that update. Check-only mode still sends notifications; recreation stays outside the app. The app container itself updates from the UI when self-update is enabled.

 Remote hosts

Agent URLs that resolve to private or reserved networks are blocked by default. The check is best-effort; see Security. The client then connects only to addresses that passed the check and keeps the original hostname, so TLS and virtual hosts stay intact. A remote agent on a LAN or a Docker network is allowed with AGENT ALLOW NETWORKS (for example 192.168.0.0/24 ) and/or AGENT ALLOW ENDPOINTS (for example 10.0.0.5:9413 ). See .env.example. With AGENT ENABLED=true , only 127.0.0.1:8001 is allowed until an exception is set.

A remote host runs the agent, from docker-compose.agent.yml or from:

 

The host is added under Menu → Hosts. The agent secret matches AGENT SECRET on the agent container. Backend and agent speak HTTP. A reverse proxy can terminate HTTPS.

 Setup Host URL SSL Custom CA 
 -------------------------- ----------- --- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 Public CA on empty 
 Private CA or self-signed on CA PEM, or the self-signed certificate. The hostname or SAN matches the URL host. 
 TLS on the agent, no proxy on Cert and key mounted into the agent; --ssl-certfile and --ssl-keyfile via command (see docker-compose.agent.yml). The image healthcheck calls and fails when the agent serves only HTTPS. 

 Runtime compatibility

Tugtainer communicates directly with container runtime HTTP APIs over Unix domain sockets or TCP (including socket-proxy).

- Docker Engine : Minimum supported Docker Engine is 24.0 (Docker API 1.43 ). Docker 24 is out of upstream support; a current Engine is recommended. Version negotiation selects the highest supported API version up to the maximum tested API version 1.48 . A setting that needs a newer API is refused with a clear error before the original container is stopped.
- Podman : Rootless Podman needs DOCKER HOST=unix://$XDG RUNTIME DIR/podman/podman.sock or that socket mounted into the container. There is no automatic detection and no fallback to the rootful socket.

 Socket proxy

The app and the agent can run without a direct Docker socket mount. The provided Compose files do this by default. Example proxy: linuxserver/socket-proxy.

 Feature Proxy variables 
 --------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 Discovery & Health VERSION=1 , PING=1 , INFO=1 
 Check CONTAINERS=1 , IMAGES=1 , POST=1 
 Update & Recreation CONTAINERS=1 , IMAGES=1 , NETWORKS=1 , POST=1 
 Logs ALLOW LOGS=1 
 Hooks & Exec EXEC=1 , POST=1 
 Start, stop, restart, pause ALLOW START=1 , ALLOW STOP=1 , ALLOW RESTARTS=1 , ALLOW PAUSE=1 , ALLOW UNPAUSE=1 
 Swarm SERVICES=1 , TASKS=1 , NODES=1 , SWARM=1 , DISTRIBUTION=1 

 DOCKER HOST on the app or the agent points at the proxy, for example tcp://my-socket-proxy:port . Supported schemes are unix:// , tcp:// , and ssh:// is rejected. A non-empty DOCKER TLS VERIFY turns tcp:// into HTTPS and verifies the daemon with ca.pem , cert.pem , and key.pem . The directory is DOCKER CERT PATH , otherwise DOCKER CONFIG , otherwise /.docker . Missing or invalid certificate files fail at connection time. together with DOCKER TLS VERIFY is rejected.

The Compose files leave EXEC commented out. Uncomment it on a host where update hooks should run. Hooks also need ALLOW HOOKS on the app and ALLOW EXEC on the agent.

 Environment

Most variables are optional. AGENT SECRET is required. The full list is in .env.example.

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
The app starts from docker-compose.app.yml or from:

docker volume create tugtainer_data

docker pull ghcr.io/quenary/tugtainer:2

# AGENT_SECRET is required. Set a strong, unique shared secret.
docker run -d -p 9412:80 \
    --name=tugtainer \
    --restart=unless-stopped \
    -e AGENT_SECRET="" \
    -v tugtainer_data:/tugtainer \
    -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro \
    ghcr.io/quenary/tugtainer:2

On the first start the container logs a one-time setup code (docker logs tugtainer). The password is set with that code within 5 minutes. An expired code requires a restart. See Auth.

The app cannot update an agent or a socket-proxy: those containers carry the Docker API connection. A Compose project that mixes them with containers set to auto-update fails that update. Check-only mode still sends notifications; recreation stays outside the app. The app container itself updates from the UI when self-update is enabled.
